estimate.damage_summary: An atmospheric overvoltage event damaged the plugged-in speaker system and TV. A technician attended afterward to confirm the surge failure and check the wiring; no surge-protection device was used.
estimate.policy_notes: The damaged appliances are covered for lightning-related overvoltage under clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4, subject to the EUR 5,000 gross appliance sub-limit and the pre-loss-standard cap in 7.1.9. Because the description establishes that no surge-protection device was used, clause 2.3.3 halves the indemnity for the damaged appliances. Delivery and putting replacement equipment into service are excluded by 7.1.8(b)–(c); diagnostic, report and administrative/order charges are excluded by 7.1.8(e)–(f), and call-out is payable only alongside indemnifiable work under 7.1.8(d).

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: Clauses 2.3.3 and 4.2.4 cover appliances physically damaged by the established overvoltage event, subject to the appliance sub-limit; clause 7.1.9 limits replacement to the pre-loss standard. The line is predominantly replacement equipment, but any bundled delivery or putting into service is excluded under 7.1.8(b)–(c); the missing surge protector halves the otherwise payable amount under 2.3.3. Two appliances are consistent with the reported damage, but their models and former specifications are not given.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: The attendance relates to the reported surge event, but the diagnostic/report charge is the contractor's own diagnostic work excluded by 7.1.8(e), and the claim-specific description also identifies arrangement/order charges excluded by 7.1.8(f). Under 7.1.8(d), call-out is not payable where the invoice work is not indemnifiable; the description establishes one attendance, not three. The line is therefore excluded despite being event-related.
